00:05:08	terence:	here's an attempt of DC on top of PQ: https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/compare/pq...pq-dc a few open questions:
head vote proofs / aggregation. If head vote aggregation takes time, view merge becomes pointless. Combine head vote proof with finality vote proof into one STARK proof?
FG vote aggregation scheme. Round vs epoch, target vs timeout, what's supported / not supported?
FG attestation uses 1 leaf per round. Voting target -> timeout in the same round reuses the leaf and exposes the key. Fix attestation field to use slot/epoch?
builder payments across slots via old head votes. This can get very expensive. Can we get rid of it and lose trustless payment protection?

00:06:50	Justin Traglia:	Instead of initiating exits of unregistered validators, we immediately exit them but set a very long withdrawal delay of 16,384 epochs (~72 days). Unregistered validators will not be able to perform duties after the fork; therefore there shouldn't be missed proposals nor a large drop in attestation participation.

00:18:18	Justin Traglia:	The reduction of MAX_COMMITTEES_PER_SLOT from 64 committees to 16 committees. This mirrors the earlier reduction of ATTESTATION_SUBNET_COUNT from 64 subnets to 16 subnets. So now there's one committee per subnet again. These changes increase the amount of data propagated on per subnet, but will result in fewer aggregations (300 KiB proofs) in the beacon_aggregate_and_proof topic which is a necessary tradeoff.
00:19:23	Justin Traglia:	Aggregators no longer select themselves with VRF selection proofs. Instead, each beacon committee has an aggregation committee, sampled by effective balance. The committee is stored in a new aggregation_committee_window field within the state, like the proposer lookahead and PTC window. This means that every committee now has exactly four aggregators, rather than a random number that is sometimes zero.
00:22:25	Justin Traglia:	To reduce traffic on the beacon_aggregate_and_proof topic, only the "best" aggregates are propagated. The best aggregate is defined as the aggregate which contains attestations with the most effective balance; an aggregate with an attestation from a single 65 ETH validator is better than an aggregate with attestations from two 32 ETH validators. Late aggregates are judged the same as today though, which may include some late attestations.
